newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower ahead of June expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower ahead of June expiry.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open lower Wednesday ahead of June's expiry this afternoon, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.32 to $2.34 after settling to the upside Tuesday at $2.363 per million British thermal units.
OTC is consistent with the ACCESS session, where June last traded 1.9 cents lower at $2.34.
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked two to four cents firmer at $2.32-2.34 as hot, humid weather in Texas and the Southwest sustained a strong cooling demand.

Temperatures in Houston, Texas, are forecast to reach a high of about 90 degrees F today, with relative humidity hovering around 76 percent. Highs in the high-80s are expected over the next few days, but the humidity level is forecast to drop this weekend to about 50 percent, according to Weather Services Corp.
Cooler-than-normal weather is expected to blanket most of the East and Midwest through this week's end before returning to near-normal this weekend and into early next week, WSC also said.
Technically, traders said resistance in June was at $2.40 and then at the $2.43 contract high, while support was pegged at $2.27 and $2.25.

Taking a look ahead, traders saw July support at $2.30 and the low-$2.20s. Resistance was pegged at $2.38 and then at the contract high of $2.44. July support was pegged first at $2.30, with trendline support in the low-$2.20s.

In Tuesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed by about 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes were up an equal amount to about $2.10. New York city gate gas gained about five cents to the high-$2.40s.
Meanwhile, injection estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from about 70 to 80 bcf, versus a gain of 83 bcf a year ago.
